monthly_review.summary: You've significantly increased training volume and intensity this month, with faster paces, higher HR, and more time in Zones 3–4 — indicating a deliberate shift toward threshold and aerobic capacity development.
monthly_review.highlight: Zone distribution shifted dramatically: Zone 3 time increased from 19% to 31%, and Zone 4 rose from 3% to 15%, reflecting intentional higher-intensity work — but at the cost of reduced Z1/Z2 recovery volume.

goal_tracker.message: You’ve already exceeded last month’s total distance (61.0 km vs. 46.0 km) and number of runs (11 vs. 10). No additional km is needed — use the remaining 2 days for active recovery or optional low-impact cross-training to support adaptation.

insights.title: Efficiency improved despite higher intensity
insights.body: Aerobic efficiency rose slightly from 13.42 to 13.46 m/sec per bpm, even as average HR increased +4 bpm and Zone 3/4 time grew — suggesting better cardiovascular coupling during harder efforts.

insights.title: Recovery volume dropped sharply
insights.body: Time in Z1+Z2 fell from 79% (36%+43%) last month to 53% (24%+29%) this month — well below the 80% minimum recommended for sustainable aerobic base development in recreational runners.

insights.title: Cadence and stride length both improved under load
insights.body: Avg cadence rose +5 spm (146→151), and recent runs show stride length increasing from 63.3 m (slow 3.2 km @ 10:50/km) to 72.2 m (faster 6.5 km @ 8:56/km), indicating better neuromuscular coordination at pace.

insights.title: Ground contact time decreased with pace
insights.body: Ground contact time dropped from 344 ms (3.2 km @ 10:50/km) to 312 ms (6.5 km @ 8:56/km), aligning with faster pace and improved efficiency — but vertical oscillation remained stable (7.2–7.9 cm), suggesting no wasted energy increase.

recommendations.action: Do one 45-min Zone 2 run (HR 125–135 bpm) before month-end — aim for avg HR ≤133 bpm and cadence ≥148 spm.
recommendations.reason: Your Z1+Z2 volume dropped 26 percentage points this month; this session restores critical aerobic stimulus without fatigue accumulation.

recommendations.action: Perform a 6 km progression run: first 2 km @ 9:30/km (HR ~138), middle 2 km @ 9:00/km (HR ~144), final 2 km @ 8:45/km (HR ~148–150).
recommendations.reason: Recent runs show you can sustain 8:56/km (6.5 km) and 9:23/km (11.0 km); this builds race-specific stamina while staying within your observed HR ceiling of 149 bpm.

recommendations.action: After your next run >5 km, do 3×1-min barefoot strides on grass focusing on quiet footstrike and knee lift — monitor vertical oscillation trend in Garmin post-run.
recommendations.reason: Vertical oscillation held steady (7.2–7.9 cm) despite faster paces — targeted neuromuscular drills will reinforce efficient posture and reduce ground contact time further.

weekly_focus.description: Balance higher-intensity work with disciplined Zone 2 pacing to rebuild recovery capacity while sharpening your ability to hold goal marathon/half-marathon pace efficiently.
